q: $\text{X(aq)} \rightarrow \text{products}$ is first order in X. Starting at $[\text{X}] = 1.0\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$, the half-life is $16$ minutes. What is the half-life if you start at $2.0\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$?
qShort: First order · $t_{1/2} = 16$ min at $1.0$ · half-life at $2.0$?

lines.say: A first-order reaction has a half-life of sixteen minutes when it starts at one mole per decimetre cubed. {dbl}Double the starting concentration. What's the half-life now?
This is a real OCR A-level question. Pause and have a go!
Okay! {c1}Here's the reaction starting at one. {h1}It halves every sixteen minutes.
Now start at two. {c2}After sixteen minutes, it's down to one. {shift}And from there, it's exactly the same curve as before!
{h}So it still halves every sixteen minutes. For a first-order reaction, the half-life doesn't depend on concentration. {ans}It's D, sixteen minutes.
If you said eight, {rate}you spotted that the rate doubles. {amt}But twice as much has to react, so the time stays the same.
